Description

The chemokine CCL2 binds its receptor CCR2 on nociceptors. CCR2 couples to Gi, and the Gβγ dimer released from Gi raises the current of the sodium channel NaV1.8, which contributes substantially to the action potential upstroke in small sensory neurons. A CCR2 antagonist, pertussis toxin and the Gβγ inhibitor gallein each prevent this rise. After destabilisation of the medial meniscus in mice, CCL2 and CCR2 increase in the dorsal root ganglia that innervate the knee. Mice lacking CCR2 have the same joint damage but do not develop movement-provoked pain.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: CCR2 raises pain through Gβγ acting on NaV1.8.
